name: fairy ointment

attributes.attribute: lets a viewer see things as they truly are

sources: Curtin, Jeremiah. Hero-Tales of Ireland. (New York: Benjamin Blom, 1894), 156.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy ointment is a folkloric motif. It is a salve made in Fairyland, perhaps pressed from the oil of clover leaves or shamrocks. It lets a viewer see things as they truly are. In tales of the fairy midwife, a midwife told to rub the ointment on a newborn's eyes touched her own eye by accident. She then saw a broken hut where a palace had stood just before. The ointment changed her sight for good. She could see through fairy glamour and see the fairies themselves. The fairies punished the theft, even if unwitting, by blinding the thief.

okr.objective: Fairy ointment is a folkloric salve that grants true sight.
